title: The Tenets of Our Faith · Scripture Challenge

slides.title: THE TENETS OF OUR FAITH
slides.sub: A Scripture challenge · Oneness · Holiness · New Birth
slides.notes: Welcome. Ask before explaining. Do not reveal the answers before the congregation responds. Two QR codes for study participation and Apostolic Guide appear on the cover. A larger scan slide is next.

slides.title: SCAN TO JOIN THE STUDY
slides.sub: Follow the teaching, vote in live polls, and send questions. Keep learning with Apostolic Guide.
slides.notes: Display before the warm-up poll. Give everyone a moment to scan the LEFT code, enter their email and open the live lesson. The RIGHT code opens apostolicguide.com for independent follow-up Bible study. Both codes also appear at the end. This slide can be taken again at any time from the iPad manuscript.

slides.title: Do you know what you believe, or only what you were taught?
slides.sub: If someone asks you WHY, can you explain it from Scripture?
slides.notes: Poll first, then invite two people to explain their choices.

slides.title: The rules of the challenge
points: One person reads the objection aloud.
Someone offers the strongest opposing interpretation.
Someone offers an Apostolic response.
We read the larger passage, not a detached verse.
We mark: text, interpretation, and unresolved questions.

slides.title: One God is the starting point
slides.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD:
slides.notes: Connect with Mark 12:29; Isaiah 44:6 and 45:5; do not assert this verse alone disproves the Trinity.

slides.title: CHALLENGE 1 · Who is “US”?
slides.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
slides.notes: SHOW ONLY verse 26. Do not hint at verse 27 yet. Have someone offer a fair Trinitarian reading, then ask: Who actually creates in the following verse?

slides.title: THE ANSWER · Keep reading
slides.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
slides.notes: Read the whole verse three times slowly: God, HIS, HE. Emphasize text vs theological conclusion.

slides.title: “US” spoke. HE created.
points: Verse 26: “Let US make … OUR image.”
Verse 27: “So GOD created … HIS own image.”
Verse 27: “In the image of God created HE him.”
The action is attributed to God in the singular.
slides.notes: The reveal is the contrast. Avoid claiming verse 27 rules out every Trinitarian reading: classic Trinitarians agree that the one God created.

slides.title: CHALLENGE 2 · Two LORDs?
slides.text: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;
slides.notes: Ask them to identify subject, verb, what fell and where it came from. Can the same name be repeated without positing two divine persons?

slides.title: RE-PUNCTUATE THE READING
slides.sub: Brackets and rewording represent interpretations, NOT the original Hebrew text.
slides.notes: Important: Do not claim commas prove the one-LORD reading. The Hebrew repeats the divine name; both approaches must explain it.
slides.left:
TWO-PERSON INTERPRETATION
The LORD [on earth] rained fire from the LORD [in heaven].
slides.right:
ONE-LORD PARAPHRASE
The LORD caused fire to rain from heaven, as the LORD's judgment.

slides.title: CHALLENGE 3 · Who is speaking?
points: v12 · “I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.”
v13 · “Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth.”
v14 · “The LORD hath loved him … his pleasure on Babylon.”
v15 · “I, even I, have spoken … I have called him.”
slides.notes: Identify the LORD as speaker in 12–15. Have the room track the verbs and who 'I' means. Then display 16 unchanged.

slides.title: Read Isaiah 48:16 without quotation marks
slides.text: Come ye near unto me, hear ye this; I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me.
slides.notes: First present without our red/blue markers. Ask: If 'I' is the same throughout, how does the sending language sound?

slides.title: WHERE WOULD YOU CLOSE THE QUOTE?
slides.sub: Read to “…there am I:” · At “AND NOW,” is the speaker still the LORD, or does Isaiah begin speaking?
slides.notes: Take three responses. This is the Instagram quotation-marker challenge. Next screen reveals the user's red/blue LORD/ISAIAH structure.

slides.title: 🔴 LORD · 🔵 ISAIAH
slides.sub: Speaker labels and quotation marks are OUR reading aids, not marks in the Hebrew manuscript.
points: 🔴 LORD (vv12–15): “I am the first … I also am the last.”
🔴 LORD (v16a): “...from the time that it was, there am I.”
🔵 ISAIAH (v16b): “And now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me.”
🔵 ISAIAH (v17a): “Thus saith the LORD, thy Redeemer ...”
🔴 LORD (v17b): “I am the LORD thy God ...”
slides.notes: Recreate Instagram pattern: NOW, FROM THIS BLUE DOT TO THE NEXT BLUE DOT, ISAIAH. Blue voice introduces Thus saith the LORD; within it the LORD's quotation resumes.

slides.title: Who is the “ME”?
points: Our reading: v16b is Isaiah speaking of his commission.
The red LORD quotation ends after “there am I.”
The blue prophetic voice starts at “And now ... hath sent me.”
“Thus saith the LORD” in v17 introduces God's words again.
The text does not explicitly identify three eternal persons.
slides.notes: Own the objection: speaker transition isn't tagged 'Isaiah said', so the alternative isn't demonstrably impossible. Speak with careful confidence.

slides.title: CHALLENGE 4 · The Word was WITH God
slides.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
slides.notes: State the doctrine fairly: the Logos is the eternal Son, personally with the Father, fully God, not a second God. Ask how the same Bible describes God's speech in creation.

slides.title: HOW DID GOD CREATE?
slides.sub: Every time you hear ‘And God said,’ call it out. Who speaks? Who brings it into being?
slides.notes: Open Genesis 1:1–12. Make the audience track repeated God said/God made/God called. The next slides reveal the actual sequence.

slides.title: GENESIS 1:1–3 · GOD CREATES AND SPEAKS
points: v1 · “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.”
v2 · “And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.”
v3 · “And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.”
slides.notes: Read the complete verses on your iPad manuscript. The slide quotes from KJV. One Creator; His Spirit; His speech.

slides.title: GENESIS 1:4–6 · GOD CALLS AND SPEAKS
points: v4 · “And God saw the light, that it was good.”
v5 · “And God called the light Day ...”
v6 · “And God said, Let there be a firmament ...”
slides.notes: Highlight same grammatical subject, God. Invite congregation to repeat 'God said' when v6 is read.

slides.title: GENESIS 1:7–9 · GOD MAKES AND SPEAKS
points: v7 · “And God made the firmament ... and it was so.”
v8 · “And God called the firmament Heaven.”
v9 · “And God said, Let the waters ... and it was so.”
slides.notes: Ask: if 'God said' and 'God made' alternate, what does that reveal about speech and act?

slides.title: GENESIS 1:10–12 · HE SPOKE. IT WAS SO.
points: v10 · “And God called the dry land Earth ...”
v11 · “And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass ... and it was so.”
v12 · “And the earth brought forth ... and God saw that it was good.”
slides.notes: Now ask what John 1:1 means within the Jewish Bible, and transition to Isaiah 44:24.

slides.title: “ALONE … BY MYSELF”
slides.text: Thus saith the LORD, thy redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb, I am the LORD that maketh all things; that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth by myself;
slides.notes: Underline alone and by myself. Ask a Trinitarian how they read the same verse: they also hold one Creator, through the eternal Word. Don't say this verse by itself disproves Trinity.

slides.title: THE WORD WAS GOD. THE WORD BECAME FLESH.
points: God spoke. God created. God made. God called.
His Word was WITH Him, and His Word WAS God.
The one LORD says: “I ... stretched forth the heavens alone.”
John 1:14: That Word was made flesh.
Jesus Christ reveals the one God, not a second God.
slides.notes: This is our theological reading. Do not claim the Genesis 'God said' motif alone disproves an eternal Logos-person reading.

slides.title: FOUR OBJECTIONS. ONE GOD.
slides.sub: Keep reading. Follow the speaker. Identify the Creator. Let Scripture interpret Scripture.
slides.notes: Ask four volunteers: one sentence per challenge. Then move on to Holiness.

slides.title: HOLINESS · Is holiness mostly about clothing?
slides.sub: 'Holiness is why we do it. Modesty is how we do it.' Is that the whole picture?

slides.title: Be holy in all manner of life
slides.text: But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;

slides.title: HEAD COVERING · Why does Paul mention angels?
slides.sub: If it were only about other people seeing us, why 'because of the angels'?
slides.notes: No invented details about exactly what angels do. Read 3–16 including 11–12 and 15.

slides.title: Because of the angels
slides.text: For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.

slides.title: Her hair is given for a covering
slides.text: But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.

slides.title: BAPTISM · What is the 'name'?
slides.sub: Jesus says 'in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.' What did the apostles actually say and do?

slides.title: Go, baptizing in the name
slides.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:

slides.title: What does ONOMA actually mean?
slides.sub: Jesus says all POWER is His, then commands baptism in the NAME. Are those the same Greek word?
slides.notes: Ask first. Launch the Greek poll on the iPad. Let the church distinguish the two words before revealing.

slides.title: ONOMA ≠ EXOUSIA
slides.sub: The name identifies the person; the commission carries His authority.
points: ὄνομα (onoma) = name; can imply identity and represented authority.
εἰς τὸ ὄνομα (eis to onoma) = into the name (v.19).
ἐξουσία (exousia) = authority, rendered “power” in KJV v.18.
The baptismal phrase is not literally “in the power of.”
slides.notes: Do not let the etymology overstate a baptismal conclusion; move from grammar to the Acts narrative.

slides.title: There is none other name
slides.sub: Read Acts 3:6 and 4:7–12 to identify which name Peter means.
slides.text: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
slides.notes: Ask: whose name had Peter used to heal the lame man? Compare Acts 3:6, 4:10, 4:12.

slides.title: Repent and be baptized
slides.text: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.

slides.title: HOLY GHOST · How do you know you received?
slides.sub: Is it a feeling? A raised hand? Speaking in tongues? The Spirit's ongoing fruit?

slides.title: As the Spirit gave utterance
slides.text: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

slides.title: They heard them speak with tongues
slides.text: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,

slides.title: What does the new birth call us to?
points: Repent: turn to God in faith.
Be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
Receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
Continue in doctrine, fellowship, prayer, and holy living.
slides.notes: Close with response and open questions; don't turn Q&A into pressure toward visitors.

slides.title: CAN YOU GIVE AN ANSWER?
slides.sub: Defend your faith. Test your interpretation. Honor the person asking.
slides.notes: Take anonymous questions. End with prayer.

slides.title: KEEP STUDYING. KEEP ASKING.
slides.sub: Review the lesson and continue studying Scripture after tonight.
slides.notes: Leave this slide on screen during dismissal so audience members who came late can join the study and everyone can save Apostolic Guide.

verses.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD:
verses.text_en: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD:
verses.text_es: Oye, Israel: Jehová nuestro Dios, Jehová uno es.

verses.text: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.
verses.text_en: For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.
verses.text_es: Porque en él habita corporalmente toda la plenitud de la Deidad,

verses.text: Come ye near unto me, hear ye this; I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me.
verses.text_en: Come ye near unto me, hear ye this; I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me.
verses.text_es: Acercaos a mí, oíd esto: desde el principio no hablé en secreto; desde que eso se hizo, allí estaba yo; y ahora me envió Jehová el Señor, y su Espíritu.

verses.text: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;
verses.text_en: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;
verses.text_es: Entonces Jehová hizo llover sobre Sodoma y sobre Gomorra azufre y fuego de parte de Jehová desde los cielos;

verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
verses.text_en: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
verses.text_es: En el principio era el Verbo, y el Verbo era con Dios, y el Verbo era Dios.

verses.text: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:
verses.text_en: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:
verses.text_es: Seguid la paz con todos, y la santidad, sin la cual nadie verá al Señor.

verses.text: But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;
verses.text_en: But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;
verses.text_es: sino, como aquel que os llamó es santo, sed también vosotros santos en toda vuestra manera de vivir;

verses.text: For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.
verses.text_en: For this cause ought the woman to have power on her head because of the angels.
verses.text_es: Por lo cual la mujer debe tener señal de autoridad sobre su cabeza, por causa de los ángeles.

verses.text: But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.
verses.text_en: But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.
verses.text_es: Por el contrario, a la mujer dejarse crecer el cabello le es honroso; porque en lugar de velo le es dado el cabello.

verses.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
verses.text_en: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
verses.text_es: Por tanto, id, y haced discípulos a todas las naciones, bautizándolos en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo;

verses.text: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
verses.text_en: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
verses.text_es: Pedro les dijo: Arrepentíos, y bautícese cada uno de vosotros en el nombre de Jesucristo para perdón de los pecados; y recibiréis el don del Espíritu Santo.

verses.text: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.text_en: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.text_es: Cuando oyeron esto, fueron bautizados en el nombre del Señor Jesús.

verses.text: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
verses.text_en: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
verses.text_es: Y fueron todos llenos del Espíritu Santo, y comenzaron a hablar en otras lenguas, según el Espíritu les daba que hablasen.

verses.text: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,
verses.text_en: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,
verses.text_es: Porque los oían que hablaban en lenguas, y que magnificaban a Dios.

verses.text: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
verses.text_en: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
verses.text_es: Y habiéndoles impuesto Pablo las manos, vino sobre ellos el Espíritu Santo; y hablaban en lenguas, y profetizaban.

verses.text: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
verses.text_en: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
verses.text_es: Respondió Jesús: De cierto, de cierto te digo, que el que no naciere de agua y del Espíritu, no puede entrar en el reino de Dios.

verses.text: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
verses.text_en: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
verses.text_es: Y Jesús se acercó y les habló diciendo: Toda potestad me es dada en el cielo y en la tierra.

verses.text: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
verses.text_en: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
verses.text_es: Y en ningún otro hay salvación; porque no hay otro nombre bajo el cielo, dado a los hombres, en que podamos ser salvos.

verses.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
verses.text_en: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
verses.text_es: Entonces dijo Dios: Hagamos al hombre a nuestra imagen, conforme a nuestra semejanza; y señoree en los peces del mar, en las aves de los cielos, en las bestias, en toda la tierra, y en todo animal que se arrastra sobre la tierra.

verses.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
verses.text_en: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
verses.text_es: Y creó Dios al hombre a su imagen, a imagen de Dios lo creó; varón y hembra los creó.

verses.text: Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.
verses.text_en: Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.
verses.text_es: Óyeme, Jacob, y tú, Israel, a quien llamé: Yo mismo, yo el primero, yo también el postrero.

verses.text: Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens: when I call unto them, they stand up together.
verses.text_en: Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens: when I call unto them, they stand up together.
verses.text_es: Mi mano fundó también la tierra, y mi mano derecha midió los cielos con el palmo; al llamarlos yo, comparecieron juntamente.

verses.text: All ye, assemble yourselves, and hear; which among them hath declared these things? The LORD hath loved him: he will do his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans.
verses.text_en: All ye, assemble yourselves, and hear; which among them hath declared these things? The LORD hath loved him: he will do his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans.
verses.text_es: Juntaos todos vosotros, y oíd. ¿Quién hay entre ellos que anuncie estas cosas? Aquel a quien Jehová amó ejecutará su voluntad en Babilonia, y su brazo estará sobre los caldeos.

verses.text: I, even I, have spoken; yea, I have called him: I have brought him, and he shall make his way prosperous.
verses.text_en: I, even I, have spoken; yea, I have called him: I have brought him, and he shall make his way prosperous.
verses.text_es: Yo, yo hablé, y le llamé y le traje; por tanto, será prosperado su camino.

verses.text: Thus saith the LORD, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.
verses.text_en: Thus saith the LORD, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.
verses.text_es: Así ha dicho Jehová, Redentor tuyo, el Santo de Israel: Yo soy Jehová Dios tuyo, que te enseña provechosamente, que te encamina por el camino que debes seguir.

verses.text: Thus saith the LORD, thy redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb, I am the LORD that maketh all things; that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth by myself;
verses.text_en: Thus saith the LORD, thy redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb, I am the LORD that maketh all things; that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth by myself;
verses.text_es: Así dice Jehová, tu Redentor, que te formó desde el vientre: Yo Jehová, que lo hago todo, que extiendo solo los cielos, que extiendo la tierra por mí mismo;

verses.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
verses.text_en: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
verses.text_es: Y aquel Verbo fue hecho carne, y habitó entre nosotros (y vimos su gloria, gloria como del unigénito del Padre), lleno de gracia y de verdad.

verses.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
verses.text_en: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
verses.text_es: En el principio creó Dios los cielos y la tierra.

verses.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
verses.text_en: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
verses.text_es: Y la tierra estaba desordenada y vacía, y las tinieblas estaban sobre la faz del abismo, y el Espíritu de Dios se movía sobre la faz de las aguas.

verses.text: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
verses.text_en: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
verses.text_es: Y dijo Dios: Sea la luz; y fue la luz.

verses.text: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
verses.text_en: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
verses.text_es: Y vio Dios que la luz era buena; y separó Dios la luz de las tinieblas.

verses.text: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.
verses.text_en: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.
verses.text_es: Y llamó Dios a la luz Día, y a las tinieblas llamó Noche. Y fue la tarde y la mañana un día.

verses.text: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.
verses.text_en: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.
verses.text_es: Luego dijo Dios: Haya expansión en medio de las aguas, y separe las aguas de las aguas.

verses.text: And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.
verses.text_en: And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.
verses.text_es: E hizo Dios la expansión, y separó las aguas que estaban debajo de la expansión, de las aguas que estaban sobre la expansión. Y fue así.

verses.text: And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.
verses.text_en: And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.
verses.text_es: Y llamó Dios a la expansión Cielos. Y fue la tarde y la mañana el día segundo.

verses.text: And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.
verses.text_en: And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.
verses.text_es: Dijo también Dios: Júntense las aguas que están debajo de los cielos en un lugar, y descúbrase lo seco. Y fue así.

verses.text: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
verses.text_en: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
verses.text_es: Y llamó Dios a lo seco Tierra, y a la reunión de las aguas llamó Mares. Y vio Dios que era bueno.

verses.text: And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.
verses.text_en: And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.
verses.text_es: Después dijo Dios: Produzca la tierra hierba verde, hierba que dé semilla; árbol de fruto que dé fruto según su género, que su semilla esté en él, sobre la tierra. Y fue así.

verses.text: And the earth brought forth grass, and herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed was in itself, after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

manuscript.title: THE TENETS OF OUR FAITH
manuscript.html:
Introduction: Tonight, you are going to do some of the work. I am going to give you passages that people use to challenge what we believe. You must read them, explain their context, and make a case. No answer wins because it sounds confident.

Our pattern is Question → Read → Debate → Reveal → Explain → Apply. Faith deserves careful study and a gracious defense (Acts 17:11; 1 Peter 3:15; 2 Timothy 2:24–25).
manuscript.notes: Welcome. Ask before explaining. Do not reveal the answers before the congregation responds. Two QR codes for study participation and Apostolic Guide appear on the cover. A larger scan slide is next.

manuscript.title: SCAN TO JOIN THE STUDY
manuscript.html:
Invite the audience to participate: Two QR codes are on screen. The left code opens tonight's Doctrine Night study, with the lesson selected automatically. Scan it on your phone to follow along, vote in polls and submit anonymous questions. A valid email is required to enter the audience page; questions appear anonymously to the teacher.

The right QR code opens https://apostolicguide.com/ so people can continue their Bible study after the meeting.

Direct audience URL: https://theministry.vercel.app/class?lesson=doctrine-night-tenets-2026-10-20

Allow a moment for scanning before beginning the warm-up question.
manuscript.notes: Display before the warm-up poll. Give everyone a moment to scan the LEFT code, enter their email and open the live lesson. The RIGHT code opens apostolicguide.com for independent follow-up Bible study. Both codes also appear at the end. This slide can be taken again at any time from the iPad manuscript.

manuscript.title: Do you know what you believe, or only what you were taught?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: How do you respond when another Christian makes a biblical objection to our doctrine?

Our task is to represent an objection accurately, not to mock it. Classical Trinitarians teach ONE God in three eternally distinct persons, not three gods. We believe the one God is fully manifested in Jesus Christ. The disagreement is about God's personal distinctions, not whether Christians believe in one God.
manuscript.notes: Poll first, then invite two people to explain their choices.

manuscript.title: The rules of the challenge
manuscript.html: We do not claim every passage settles the Trinity debate on its own. Distinction in language is not automatically distinction of eternal persons. But demonstrating an alternative interpretation does not automatically prove Oneness either. Test how well your interpretation accounts for the whole biblical witness.

manuscript.title: One God is the starting point
manuscript.html:
Read Mark 12:29, Isaiah 44:6 and Isaiah 45:5. Both Apostolic Oneness and classical Trinitarian Christians affirm biblical monotheism. What differs is whether Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are eternally distinct persons within that one divine being.

Oneness starting claim: God is one, and Jesus fully reveals the one God (John 1:14; Colossians 2:9). The Son is truly human as well as truly divine. His human prayers and obedience are genuine.
manuscript.notes: Connect with Mark 12:29; Isaiah 44:6 and 45:5; do not assert this verse alone disproves the Trinity.

manuscript.title: CHALLENGE 1 · Who is “US”?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: Why does God say 'Let US make man in OUR image'? Who is 'us'?

A common Trinitarian reading sees intra-divine deliberation among Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Trinitarians do NOT teach three independent gods creating three people. Ask the congregation to identify the grammatical shift they would need to see before drawing conclusions. Do not reveal 1:27 until the next cue.
manuscript.notes: SHOW ONLY verse 26. Do not hint at verse 27 yet. Have someone offer a fair Trinitarian reading, then ask: Who actually creates in the following verse?

manuscript.title: THE ANSWER · Keep reading
manuscript.html:
READ IT: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

Question: Verse 26 says us/our. Verse 27 says God created ... HIS own image ... HE created. The narrative attributes the action to the one God.

Oneness response: The 'us' is not, by itself, a list of three persons. The next line attributes creation to God in the singular. Other proposed readings of the plural include divine-council address, deliberative or majestic speech, and the Trinitarian intra-divine reading. Verse 27 weighs against treating verse 26 as proof of multiple creators, but Trinitarians also affirm one Creator. This is evidence to weigh, not a complete disproof of the Trinity.
manuscript.notes: Read the whole verse three times slowly: God, HIS, HE. Emphasize text vs theological conclusion.

manuscript.title: “US” spoke. HE created.
manuscript.html:
Say: “Someone might stop at Let us make and say, 'See, there must be three persons.' My first answer is simple: keep reading. The next verse says, 'So GOD created man in HIS own image ... HE created him.' The sacred writer does not introduce three creators.”

Ask: Does this prove whom God addressed? No. It tells us the story's action is attributed to God, and it calls us to interpret the plural without abandoning the Bible's monotheism. Isaiah 44:24 will later emphasize God's sole creative action.
manuscript.notes: The reveal is the contrast. Avoid claiming verse 27 rules out every Trinitarian reading: classic Trinitarians agree that the one God created.

manuscript.title: CHALLENGE 2 · Two LORDs?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: If the LORD rained fire FROM the LORD, doesn't the verse describe two LORDs?

A Trinitarian can read this as a distinction between the LORD appearing on earth and the LORD in heaven. Our reading treats it as one LORD sending judgment from heaven; the repeated name emphasizes its source. Read the actual wording before proposing interpretive punctuation.
manuscript.notes: Ask them to identify subject, verb, what fell and where it came from. Can the same name be repeated without positing two divine persons?

manuscript.title: RE-PUNCTUATE THE READING
manuscript.html:
Read KJV again: Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;

Offer two readings. The first infers two personal referents when 'LORD' is repeated. The second reads one divine actor/source in a name-repetition construction: “The LORD rained judgment from heaven, from the LORD.” Both are attempts to construe the same Hebrew sentence.

Punctuation exercise: Insert oral pauses at different places without changing words, then test the meaning. Ancient Hebrew does not come with our English commas identifying how many persons are meant. Modern punctuation and square brackets on this slide are interpretive annotations; repetition by itself does not establish two eternal persons.

Read Genesis 18–19 if challenged about the earthly appearance; do not ignore the context. Our defense: repeated YHWH can emphasize authority/source without requiring two distinct persons. It does not prove one referent to everyone's satisfaction, but it certainly does not spell out Father and Son.
manuscript.notes: Important: Do not claim commas prove the one-LORD reading. The Hebrew repeats the divine name; both approaches must explain it.

manuscript.title: CHALLENGE 3 · Who is speaking?
manuscript.html:
Read 48:12–15 in order:

v12: Hearken unto me, O Jacob and Israel, my called; I am he; I am the first, I also am the last.

v13: Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens: when I call unto them, they stand up together.

v14: All ye, assemble yourselves, and hear; which among them hath declared these things? The LORD hath loved him: he will do his pleasure on Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans.

v15: I, even I, have spoken; yea, I have called him: I have brought him, and he shall make his way prosperous.

ASK: Is the “I” in verses 12–15 God or the prophet? The voice is clearly presented as divine. Notice God says He made heaven and earth and called Cyrus/Babylon's conqueror into His purpose.
manuscript.notes: Identify the LORD as speaker in 12–15. Have the room track the verbs and who 'I' means. Then display 16 unchanged.

manuscript.title: Read Isaiah 48:16 without quotation marks
manuscript.html:
Trinitarian argument: The apparent divine voice from vv12–16a says “the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me.” One reading understands the preincarnate Son, the sending Father, and the Spirit as distinguished. This is a serious exegetical challenge, not an absurd argument.

ASK: Must the sentence's “me” still be the divine speaker? Or is there a point where Isaiah interjects that he has been sent?

Do not reveal the punctuation markers until the next cue. Original Hebrew texts did not contain modern English opening and closing quotation marks, and the speaker transition is a disputed interpretation.
manuscript.notes: First present without our red/blue markers. Ask: If 'I' is the same throughout, how does the sending language sound?

manuscript.title: WHERE WOULD YOU CLOSE THE QUOTE?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: At what exact word would you place a closing quote if the prophet begins speaking?

Our speaker-switch reading places a closing quotation after there am I (v16a) and begins Isaiah's comment at and now (v16b). Classical Trinitarians often retain the same divine or messianic speaker through the sending statement. The absence of an explicit 'Isaiah said' is a genuine challenge to our interpretation.
manuscript.notes: Take three responses. This is the Instagram quotation-marker challenge. Next screen reveals the user's red/blue LORD/ISAIAH structure.

manuscript.title: 🔴 LORD · 🔵 ISAIAH
manuscript.html:
HOW TO LEAD IT: “Now we're going to put our quotation marks into the passage, and you will see how the speaker can change.”

🔴 LORD: verses 12–15 and verse 16a. The voice: “...from the time that it was, there am I.” CLOSE THE LORD'S QUOTATION HERE.

NOW, FROM THIS BLUE DOT TO THE NEXT BLUE DOT, ISAIAH:

🔵 ISAIAH: “And now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me.” Next he introduces God as speaker: “Thus saith the LORD, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel;”

🔴 LORD: “I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee to profit...” (v17b and following).

Our explanation is that “me” in 16b refers to Isaiah, a prophet sent by the Lord GOD and His Spirit; the writer is no longer quoting the LORD at that point. This is the same red/blue-dot structure from the earlier Instagram teaching. Distinguish: placement of quotation marks is an interpretation that some translations suggest, not a claim that Isaiah wrote quotation marks in Hebrew.
manuscript.notes: Recreate Instagram pattern: NOW, FROM THIS BLUE DOT TO THE NEXT BLUE DOT, ISAIAH. Blue voice introduces Thus saith the LORD; within it the LORD's quotation resumes.

manuscript.title: Who is the “ME”?
manuscript.html:
Answer to deliver: “I am not saying that the Bible has the word 'Isaiah said' sitting there. I am saying that prophets often interject and then return to announcing God's speech. Under this reading, the 'me' is the writer Isaiah, sent by the LORD and His Spirit. That's a coherent interpretation of the chapter.”

Counterpoint: There is no explicit speaker tag at 16b and the continuous divine-speaker reading remains possible. A scholar may dispute whether the prophet, Messiah, or another prophetic servant is the speaker. The verse alone does not define three eternal persons. The apostolic defense is that the strong monotheism of Isaiah must guide what distinctions are inferred.

Question: Are we treating distinctions in sending and activity as equivalent to a proven division into persons? That is a theological step requiring argument.
manuscript.notes: Own the objection: speaker transition isn't tagged 'Isaiah said', so the alternative isn't demonstrably impossible. Speak with careful confidence.

manuscript.title: CHALLENGE 4 · The Word was WITH God
manuscript.html:
Read KJV: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

COMMON TRINITARIAN EXPLANATION: “The Word was WITH God” distinguishes the eternal Logos (the Son) personally from the Father; “the Word WAS God” affirms the Logos' full deity. Jesus is this Word incarnate (John 1:14). The Trinitarian claim is one divine nature, not two gods.

ASK: Must God's own Word be another divine person because it is 'with' Him? What does Genesis portray when God creates by speaking?
manuscript.notes: State the doctrine fairly: the Logos is the eternal Son, personally with the Father, fully God, not a second God. Ask how the same Bible describes God's speech in creation.

manuscript.title: HOW DID GOD CREATE?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: Is it God and another divine person creating, or is it the one God bringing creation into being by His Word?

Oneness reading: God speaks His own Word, the expression of His mind, will and creative agency. Trinitarians also affirm that the one God creates by His Word. This pattern supports the one Creator and sets up the debate about what it means for the Word to be 'with God.' It does not by itself establish that the Word cannot be personal.
manuscript.notes: Open Genesis 1:1–12. Make the audience track repeated God said/God made/God called. The next slides reveal the actual sequence.

manuscript.title: GENESIS 1:1–3 · GOD CREATES AND SPEAKS
manuscript.html:
READ FULL TEXT:

Genesis 1:1 In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

Genesis 1:2 And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

Genesis 1:3 And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

Point: The subject is God. God creates, His Spirit moves, God speaks, and the commanded result comes to pass. In John's prologue, this divine Word is already there in the beginning. Our Oneness account identifies this Word with God Himself as His self-expression.
manuscript.notes: Read the complete verses on your iPad manuscript. The slide quotes from KJV. One Creator; His Spirit; His speech.

manuscript.title: GENESIS 1:4–6 · GOD CALLS AND SPEAKS
manuscript.html:
READ FULL TEXT:

Genesis 1:4 And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.

Genesis 1:5 And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.

Genesis 1:6 And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.

Discussion: God sees, names, divides and speaks. No new divine creator is introduced by name when He speaks. This shows how Genesis narrates divine creation through God's command.
manuscript.notes: Highlight same grammatical subject, God. Invite congregation to repeat 'God said' when v6 is read.

manuscript.title: GENESIS 1:7–9 · GOD MAKES AND SPEAKS
manuscript.html:
READ FULL TEXT:

Genesis 1:7 And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.

Genesis 1:8 And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.

Genesis 1:9 And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.

Say: God doesn't need another god in order to speak. His Word is the effective expression of His own will. The earth obeys the one Creator who speaks.
manuscript.notes: Ask: if 'God said' and 'God made' alternate, what does that reveal about speech and act?

manuscript.title: GENESIS 1:10–12 · HE SPOKE. IT WAS SO.
manuscript.html:
READ FULL TEXT:

Genesis 1:10 And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.

Genesis 1:11 And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.

Genesis 1:12 And the earth brought forth grass, and herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed was in itself, after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

Observation: Genesis repeats God created, God said, God made, God called, God saw. When John uses the Word at creation, this pattern gives a natural way to think of divine creative speech as belonging to the one God.
manuscript.notes: Now ask what John 1:1 means within the Jewish Bible, and transition to Isaiah 44:24.

manuscript.title: “ALONE … BY MYSELF”
manuscript.html:
Read slowly: Thus saith the LORD, thy redeemer, and he that formed thee from the womb, I am the LORD that maketh all things; that stretcheth forth the heavens alone; that spreadeth abroad the earth by myself;

Oneness application: The Creator says He stretched out the heavens alone, that He spread the earth by myself. When we hear “the Word was with God,” we read it against this backdrop: the one Creator's own Word, not a second divine creator helping Him.

Fair Trinitarian answer: Trinitarians affirm this same verse and argue the Father creates through the Son within the one divine being, not with help from another god. Isaiah 44:24 strongly asserts monotheism, but which model accounts for God, His Spirit, and His Word requires more than one text.
manuscript.notes: Underline alone and by myself. Ask a Trinitarian how they read the same verse: they also hold one Creator, through the eternal Word. Don't say this verse by itself disproves Trinity.

manuscript.title: THE WORD WAS GOD. THE WORD BECAME FLESH.
manuscript.html:
PUT IT TOGETHER: “Genesis begins with one God who creates by speaking. John begins with that same creation language: 'In the beginning.' God's Word is not a rival deity. The Word is with God and is God. In verse 14, that Word becomes flesh in the man Christ Jesus. That is why Jesus fully reveals God (John 1:14; Colossians 2:9).”

Critical distinction: Trinitarians also affirm one God and one act of creation. They read the Word as the eternal Son in personal fellowship with the Father. Our position understands the Word as God's own eternal self-expression becoming flesh. We disagree over the personhood of the Logos, not whether Jesus is divine or whether God is one.
manuscript.notes: This is our theological reading. Do not claim the Genesis 'God said' motif alone disproves an eternal Logos-person reading.

manuscript.title: FOUR OBJECTIONS. ONE GOD.
manuscript.html:
Review: (1) Genesis 1:26 is not the end of the sentence; v27 says God created in HIS image. (2) Genesis 19:24 repeats the divine name, but name repetition does not force two LORDs. (3) Isaiah 48:16 can be parsed with an interjection from Isaiah beginning at 'and now'; this reading must be defended, not assumed. (4) John 1:1 needs to be read with Genesis 1 and Isaiah 44:24; God creates by His own Word, and the Word becomes flesh.

Closing statement: “We do not defend Oneness by ignoring the objections. We answer them by reading more of the Bible.”

Invite one challenge back from the class. Keep the discussion charitable and move to Holiness with this transition: “If God is one, our life belongs wholly to Him.”
manuscript.notes: Ask four volunteers: one sentence per challenge. Then move on to Holiness.

manuscript.title: HOLINESS · Is holiness mostly about clothing?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: Can someone look modest and still live unholy?

Yes. Holiness is belonging to the holy God; it governs the whole life: motive, compassion, honesty, speech, fidelity, consumption and conduct. Modesty is one outward expression of humility and restraint, not the entirety of holiness (1 Peter 1:15–16; Hebrews 12:14; 1 Timothy 2:9–10). The maxim is memorable, but holiness reaches farther than clothing.

manuscript.title: Be holy in all manner of life
manuscript.html: Read 1 Peter 1:13–16 and Hebrews 12:14. Holiness includes the inner life and outward practice. A heart claim that never alters life is deficient; an outward standard without a yielded heart is also deficient. Ask people to name non-clothing examples of holiness.

manuscript.title: HEAD COVERING · Why does Paul mention angels?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: Why is head covering spiritual and not merely a dress rule?

Paul places the practice in the context of prayer, worship, creation and headship. 'Because of the angels' explicitly places angels in his explanation, even though their exact role is not explained. One Apostolic application sees hair or covering as an outward sign of respect for divine order, not a costume for people. The exact question of whether Paul requires cloth covering, long hair, or a first-century custom is debated. Do not state that the angels require a specific hairstyle or that covering earns salvation. Read v10 in light of v5–6, v11–12, and v15.
manuscript.notes: No invented details about exactly what angels do. Read 3–16 including 11–12 and 15.

manuscript.title: Because of the angels
manuscript.html:
Read 1 Corinthians 11:3–16. Compare v10 with v15, which calls long hair a covering. Paul is discussing both the honor of worship and a visible practice. The interpretation within many Apostolic circles emphasizes uncut hair as a spiritual sign of obedience and order. Other Christians interpret an actual fabric covering, or the entire instruction as contextual. Discuss why our conviction reads the passage as it does, then separate that conviction from speculation concerning angels. Verse 10 says 'power' (authority) on her head, and scholars debate precisely what that means.

Say: 'Holiness is not performed for an audience. Our obedience is directed toward God, and Paul asks us to reckon with a spiritual dimension of worship.' Do not claim every modesty practice is explicitly tied to angels.

manuscript.title: Her hair is given for a covering
manuscript.html: Ask: If her hair is a covering, what is the relationship to the covering of verses 5–6? There are more than one serious reading. Teach the church's reasoned practice without disguising inference as quotation. Honor the mutuality Paul affirms in verses 11–12: neither is independent in the Lord.

manuscript.title: BAPTISM · What is the 'name'?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: Is Matthew 28:19 contradicted by Acts 2:38?

Apostolic Pentecostals argue that Jesus' singular 'name' is revealed as Jesus Christ and the apostles obeyed His command by baptizing in His name. Read Acts 2:38; 8:16; 10:48; 19:5. Other Christians understand Matthew 28:19 as the baptismal words commanded by Jesus and Acts' 'in Jesus' name' as identifying allegiance/authority rather than giving a spoken formula. We need to argue why we follow the apostolic pattern, not pretend the dispute is nonexistent.

manuscript.title: Go, baptizing in the name
manuscript.html: Look closely at the singular 'name' and the three designations. Ask: Which elements are explicit? Matthew mentions Father, Son and Holy Spirit. It does not explicitly spell out 'Jesus' in this verse. The Apostolic reasoning connects Jesus' revealed saving name to the apostolic practice recorded in Acts. Explain the inference plainly.

manuscript.title: What does ONOMA actually mean?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: Does the Greek word translated “name” in Matthew 28:19 literally mean “power”? If not, what does it mean, and why does the context make authority important?

Have someone read verses 18 AND 19. In verse 18 Jesus declares that all exousia (authority) has been given to Him. Verse 19 then commands baptism eis to onoma, “into the name.” Do not treat onoma as the literal Greek for power. It is the word for name, and in context a name can refer to the person, authority, and allegiance represented by that name.
manuscript.notes: Ask first. Launch the Greek poll on the iPad. Let the church distinguish the two words before revealing.

manuscript.title: ONOMA ≠ EXOUSIA
manuscript.html:
Word study: ὄνομα (onoma, pronounced ON-oh-mah) is the ordinary Greek noun for “name.” It can stand for a person's identity, standing, or authority. In Matthew 28:19 the full phrase is εἰς τὸ ὄνομα (eis to onoma), literally “into the name.” It can convey being identified with or entering allegiance to the named one. This interpretation is about how the phrase is used; it does not turn onoma into a different word.

Contrast: Matthew 28:18: πᾶσα ἐξουσία (pasa exousia) = “all authority.” KJV renders that “All power.” Exousia means authority or the right to act. The word dynamis also means power in other NT passages, but it is not the noun Jesus uses in Matthew 28:18 or 28:19.

Apostolic argument: The risen Jesus has all authority (v.18), gives the command to baptize into the singular “name” (v.19), and the apostles repeatedly baptize in the name of Jesus Christ or the Lord Jesus (Acts 2:38; 8:16; 10:48; 19:5). Our conviction is that Peter and the apostles carried out the command rather than contradicting it.

Fair counter-reading: Trinitarians also recognize the singular Greek noun onoma, but read “Father, Son, and Holy Spirit” as the wording of Jesus' baptismal command, with Acts emphasizing the authority or allegiance represented by Jesus' name. The Greek word alone does not resolve that theological dispute.
manuscript.notes: Do not let the etymology overstate a baptismal conclusion; move from grammar to the Acts narrative.

manuscript.title: There is none other name
manuscript.html:
READ IN CONTEXT: After the healing at the temple, the authorities ask in Acts 4:7, “By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?” In verse 10 Peter explicitly names Jesus Christ of Nazareth, and in verse 12 declares that salvation is in no other.

ASK: If this is the name through which salvation comes, why is the name of Jesus so central to Apostolic preaching and baptism?

Explain: Acts 4:12 is about the exclusivity of salvation in Jesus, not a stand-alone transcript of a baptismal ceremony. Link it to the recorded practice: Acts 2:38, 8:16, 10:48 and 19:5. Do not build the whole formula argument on one lexical definition.

30-second answer for the congregation: Jesus possesses all authority. Jesus commanded baptism in the singular name of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The apostles baptized in Jesus' name. Acts 4:12 identifies Jesus as the only saving name. We understand the apostolic practice as obedience to Jesus' command.
manuscript.notes: Ask: whose name had Peter used to heal the lame man? Compare Acts 3:6, 4:10, 4:12.

manuscript.title: Repent and be baptized
manuscript.html: Read Acts 2:37–39 aloud. Peter calls for repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ's name for forgiveness, and promises the gift of the Holy Ghost. Compare Acts 8:16; 10:48; 19:5 and Acts 4:12. Baptism does not mechanically save through syllables; the response is to the risen Jesus in repentance and faith. Apostolic practice uses His name explicitly.

manuscript.title: HOLY GHOST · How do you know you received?
manuscript.html:
ASK THE ROOM: What is the biblical evidence when someone initially receives the Holy Ghost?

Classical Apostolic Pentecostal teaching regards Spirit-given speaking in other tongues as the initial outward evidence, citing Acts 2:4, 10:44–46, and 19:6. Acts 8 describes an observable result without directly naming tongues; not every reception account gives the same details. Other Christian traditions disagree that tongues is universally required. Tongues are not produced by coaching or imitation. Fruit and a transformed life are important evidence of ongoing work of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23); never confuse initial sign with total spiritual maturity.

manuscript.title: As the Spirit gave utterance
manuscript.html: Acts 2:4: the believers spoke in other tongues as the Spirit gave utterance. Acts 10:46: Gentile believers were heard speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Acts 19:6: disciples spoke in tongues and prophesied. Explain why Apostolic believers take this pattern seriously while admitting that narrative pattern and universal doctrinal requirement are not identical claims.

manuscript.title: They heard them speak with tongues
manuscript.html: Read Acts 10:44–48. The Jewish witnesses recognized the outpouring because they heard them speak with tongues and exalt God. This is a strong Pentecostal text because the narrative identifies an observable sign in the moment. Do not demand emotional theatrics. The Spirit gives utterance, not a human instructor.

manuscript.title: What does the new birth call us to?
manuscript.html: Read John 3:5 and Acts 2:38–42. This is not only an argument over formulas. We are responding to Christ's gospel. Invite sincere questions. If someone wants baptism, prayer, or further Bible study, connect them with leadership. Close by reminding the church: conviction, humility, worship, and real life must align.
manuscript.notes: Close with response and open questions; don't turn Q&A into pressure toward visitors.

manuscript.title: CAN YOU GIVE AN ANSWER?
manuscript.html:
Closing challenge: Be able to say, 'This is what the text says. This is how we understand it. Here is why. Here is the strongest question someone might still ask.' A conviction that survives an honest question becomes more than repetition.

Prayer: God, give us conviction that is rooted in Scripture, holiness that reaches the heart, and courage to obey the gospel with humility and love. Amen.
manuscript.notes: Take anonymous questions. End with prayer.

manuscript.title: KEEP STUDYING. KEEP ASKING.
manuscript.html:
Leave these links on screen during fellowship and dismissal. The left QR returns to tonight's study, and the right QR opens Apostolic Guide at https://apostolicguide.com/.
